## Contract and integration

Under the adopted text, epsilon bounds cannot replace exact QS, PR or RS
obligations. Exact cleanup, phase and coherent control remain exact. Numerical
and interval assistance is permitted when the final checked claim is an exact
proposition. Exact quotient contracts are distinguished from approximation;
no quotient or phase waiver is admitted. Internal parameters named epsilon do
not disqualify an independently admitted exact artifact's own resource bound.
Approximate source correspondence is not thereby exact source correspondence.

All fourteen criteria of [Issue #311](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/311)
are addressed by the adopted sections 1–5, the authority Reference and the
additive ledger transition. The original Constitution, three initial
interpretation records and both scoped guarantee admissions remain unchanged.
Schema v5 adds a pending supplementary interpretation across QS/PR/RS; it adds
no fourth jurisdiction and no discharged guarantee. Current evidence bindings
and the three original pending entries retain their prior contents.

The new stage protects the supplement and actual event separately from the
immutable earlier frozen-artifact manifest. Trusted-base continuity permits
the real v4-to-v5 transition and rejects rollback, incomplete stages, removed
records, fabricated discharge and altered captured bytes during verification.
Release proof disclosures include three fundamental pending interpretation IDs
and the separate EXACT ID. The constitutional checker keeps counts 3 and 1
distinct. Adoption itself does not provide the new interpretation's proofs.

Issues #31/#163 now distinguish their retained engineering approximation
requirements from exact constitutional PR/RS discharge; their implementation
criteria are not removed. #45/#120 also reference the adopted boundary.
#309 remains 0.3.1 and #310 remains v1+; neither implementation is pulled into
this work. A future edition decision remains necessary and cannot weaken
historical guarantees.

## Verification records and limits

`initial-tests-reported.json` preserves the initial actual 62 constitutional
and 26 release regression outcomes reported from the agents' tool outputs.
It is an explicit summary, not manufactured raw command output. The release
test suite's positive candidate is synthetic; no actual release passes here.

The initial release regression reproduced `KeyError: 'id'` with actual ledger
row shapes before the repair. The gate now reads pending `interpretation`
identities and requires the supplement's additional disclosure. Tests retain
different shapes for the base and supplementary rows, rather than silently
rewriting the real ledger to match the old test fixtures.

Subsequent independent review found that constitutional checking and the outer
release gate could inspect different ledger bytes yet return matching counts.
`bridge-review/` preserves the identical explicit-mock counterexample before
and after repair: the previous false ready result now rejects. The verifier
returns the digest of its captured, validated bytes; both receipt production
and consumption require that digest to match their own captured ledger. The
current release suite passes 28 tests, including missing/mismatched digests.
Its earlier 26-test result remains historical.

The final constitutional suite passes 63 tests in 127.915 seconds; its faithful
merged tool transcript and command metadata are in `final-tests/`.
Live fixed-verifier replay in `live-replay/` passes in 36.865 seconds with all
270 recorded inputs unchanged. It uses the already built Lean environment and
does not assert a new full build/audit or full constitutional Soundness.
Validation of the interpretation machinery does not discharge its mathematical
obligations or complete #141/#142. #311 is additional to the fixed original
108-Issue progress denominator.
